rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow vacatur-and-remand holding that the Oklahoma court must apply Napue/Agurs’s “any reasonable likelihood” materiality standard, treating the Attorney General’s confession as probative but not binding. Roberts is best positioned to keep the coalition together with a minimalist, federal-standard-focused opinion, while Alito likely dissents and Barrett may write separately to stress finality and the limits of confession-of-error review.
